story: A creator god and sky father descended from the sky to the land, shaping rivers, mountains, and forests throughout the lands. He then gave the people their laws of life, traditions, songs, and culture, and created the first initiation site, a sacred ground where boys were initiated into manhood. When he had finished his work, he returned to the sky, and thereafter people called him the Sky Hero, the All Father, or the Sky Father. He is said to have had two wives, one of whom is often identified with an emu, and with her he had a son, who in other tellings is instead said to be his brother. It was forbidden to speak his name publicly, and women were forbidden to view drawings of him or to approach his sacred sites, which were often male initiation grounds. In rock paintings he is depicted as a human figure with a large head-dress or hairstyle, shown always in front view with lines of footprints nearby, decorated with waistbands, vertical lines down the body, bands, and dots, while his son or brother is drawn in profile beside him. In one region, he was believed to have created all the mountains, lakes, rivers, and caves of that area. After finishing his creations there, he leapt back up into the spirit world from a particular mountain, which he flattened with his leap; its flat top remains visible to this day. A nearby cave contains rock paintings, including a large figure of a man thought to represent him, and the site is regarded as sacred.
